extractions.value: Clinical features (stiffness, spasms, hyperlordosis), EMG findings (continuous motor unit activity, exaggerated cutaneo-muscular reflexes), exclusion of mimics (myotonia, neuromyotonia, encephalomyelitis)
extractions.quote: The EMG findings, i.e. continuous activity of normal motor units and exaggerated cutaneo-muscular reflexes, not seen in other common causes of muscle tightness such as dystonia or spasticity (7), advocated in favour of SPS. Myotonia and neuromyotonia were excluded by the EMG results. Encephalomyelitis of inflammatory or paraneoplastic nature and local lesions of CNS, known to cause similar motor disturbances (1, 3), were also excluded by the absence of signs of brainstem or long tracks dysfunction and supportive laboratory results.

extractions.quote: Needle electromyography (EMG) of thigh, lower paraspinal and abdominal muscles bilaterally revealed continuous firing of normal motor unit potentials, which could not be suppressed volitionally. In addition, brief bursts of synchronous motor unit discharges were elicited in antagonist muscle pairs by unexpected sound, tap or voluntary action.

Study of cutaneo-muscular reflexes in the legs using the technique described by Meinck et al. (5), disclosed enhanced widespread responses (especially from quadriceps bilaterally) with abnormally low stimulus threshold.
